title: Safely managed sanitation, World
headline: Safely managed sanitation for all by 2030 needs coverage to rise 6.9 points a year
subtitle: Proportion of population using an improved sanitation facility that is not shared with other households, from which excreta are safely disposed of in situ or removed and treated off-site
years: So far it has risen 1.1 points a year, from 31.3% in 2000 to 58.5% in 2024.
data_line: Data: WHO/UNICEF JMP via UN SDG Global Database, series SH_SAN_SAFE, extracted 1 Nov 2026
alt: Safely managed sanitation for all by 2030 needs coverage to rise 6.9 points a year. So far it has risen 1.1 points a year, from 31.3% in 2000 to 58.5% in 2024. People using safely managed sanitation, the world: 31.3% in 2000, 58.5% in 2024. At that pace about 65.3% in 2030; reaching 100% needs 6.9 points a year.
method: Method: linear pace, 2000 to 2024; target year 2030.
question: Where has safely managed sanitation moved at anything like 6.9 points a year, and what made it possible?
